method: Reconstructed the credit grid and inspected the individual excursion, seminar, elective and thesis entries before comparing the frozen record to the workbook course content and exact-target interests.
findings: The grid independently closes at 60 EC per year. The year-two 12 EC restricted parent contains 6 EC of specialisation and 6 EC of Art History choice. Separate 12 EC field study requires completion of the Art History first year. The 36 EC year-three open space includes the possibility of a 30 EC mobility semester. The 12 EC seminar can precede the thesis, and the thesis requires first-year completion and compulsory year-two courses.

Both UCR options share sustained art study through Western art, Renaissance Italy and the Mediterranean, African art and heritage, modern museums, and methods of interpretation. The historical option adds ancient material evidence and historical and literary contexts. The contemporary option emphasises environmental imagery, protest art, television representation, contemporary social theory and public communication. Each keeps eight unique courses and all offerings and prerequisites pass.

Rechecked the strongest alignments through actual course content. UCR’s introductory survey overlaps around late-medieval art and approaches to paintings, while UvA’s first survey begins in antiquity. The UCR archaeology course and UvA techniques course both use material observation but differ in their objects and workshop practice. General historical inquiry in Researching the “American Century” does not substitute for the UvA research seminar. The optional independent research item stays alongside the thesis outside the scheduled total.

Reconciled the English title, both concept labels, 22 credited components, eight note anchors, 32 selected titles and descriptions, and source destinations. The revised notes distinguish genuine curricular choice, required field study and the depth of the thesis sequence.
